sample_unit: random skin lesion cases from PAD-UFES-20 (50 repeated trials each)

links.outcome: Comparison of GPT-4o against specialised neural networks on skin lesion malignancy triage
links.effect: Specialised neural networks significantly outperformed GPT-4o on most pairwise comparisons; GPT-4o balanced accuracies were 0.571, 0.602, 0.622 for clinical, image, multimodal inputs.
links.quote: Specialised neural networks significantly outperformed GPT-4o on most pairwise comparisons.

links.outcome: GPT-4o discriminative performance across age, sex, and skin tone subgroups
links.effect: Poorer discriminative performance in younger patients versus middle-aged and elderly; no notable differences between sex and skin tone subgroups.
links.quote: Fairness evaluations showed poorer discriminative performance in younger patients compared to middle-aged and elderly patients but no notable differences between different sex and skin tone subgroups.

links.outcome: GPT-4o output reproducibility across 50 repeated trials
links.effect: Mean agreement rates were >0.90, but Fleiss' kappa indicated only moderate consistency due to strong bias toward malignant classifications.
links.quote: Mean agreement rates were high (>0.90); however, Fleiss' κ indicated only moderate consistency due to a strong bias toward malignant classifications.

links.outcome: GPT-4o triage performance for skin lesion malignancy
links.effect: Poor triage performance; balanced accuracy 0.571-0.622, sensitivity >0.95 but very low specificity.
links.quote: Sensitivity was consistently high (>0.95) with the trade-off of very low specificity.

unlisted_practices: Multimodal (image plus clinical data) inputs improve general-purpose LLM performance over unimodal inputs

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the diagnostic performance, consistency, and fairness of GPT-4o compared to specialised neural networks on an existing dermatological dataset (PAD-UFES-20) without testing a specific deployment safeguard or practice.
